newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN RALLIES AS CBANK LEAVES RATES ALONE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN RALLIES AS CBANK LEAVES RATES ALONE.

text.p: The Czech crown rallied in late trading after heavy early losses against its dollar/market basket on Thursday, spurred by a central bank decision leaving interest rates untouched after its regular board meeting.
The Czech crown slumped by more than one full percentage point amid nervousness that the Czech National Bank (CNB) was preparing to cut interest rates.

After its weekly board meeting, the CNB announced that it was lowering minimum reserve requirements to 9.5 percent from 11.5 percent, effective May 8. But the bank did not announce a change in interest rates, allowing the crown to regain nearly half of its early losses.
"The crown gained immediately after and I expect it will hold, or maybe strenthen a little, until next week," said Viktor Mikulecky, a forex trader at Girocredit in Prague.

The crown, which is fixed daily against a mark/dollar basket, was trading at 29.642 to the dollar and 17.256 to the mark in late afternoon activity, putting it 1.20 percent above the basket mid-point after it fell one full percentage point to below +0.70.

Dealers said that while there was no rate cut on Thursday, they could not rule out the possibility that the central bank would move next week in tandem with the government which will announce a series of measures to spur the economy on April 16.
"I think the market is nervous and the nervousness could still be there till next week when the government will announce some economic measures," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka.

The economy has run into serious problems in recent months with the latest batch of bad news coming on Wednesday morning when official figures showed industrial production falling 5.8 percent year-on-year in February.

Senior government officials have been vocal in blaming the central bank's highly restrictive monetary policy for the economic slowdown and many foreign exchange dealers are still convinced that the CNB will cut rates soon.
"I think the market is more or less positioned for a drop in interest rates," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

In an effort to rein in the money supply and bring inflation down, the Czech central bank last summer raised the discount rate by one percentage point to 10.5 percent and minimum reserve requirements were increased to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent.

The moves have been successful with M2 money growth slowing to 7.8 percent in December from over 20 percent before monetary policy was tightened, and inflation dropping to 6.8 percent in February from around 10 percent a year ago.
In announcing the lower reserve requirements, the CNB said favourable movement in the country's inflation rate and money supply allowed it to move.

The sense that a rate cut might be near was also heightened when the CTK news agency quoted Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik on Thursday as saying the central bank and government agreed to coordinate their economic policies in a late night meeting.
Korous said he expected the CNB to cut rates by around 50 basis points at first, perhaps followed by further moves later in the year.
